title: The VAPT Engagement Lifecycle
description: A penetration test follows a structured five-phase methodology. Each phase feeds the next — and the whole process repeats with every new engagement.

nodes.label: Scoping
nodes.detail: Define targets, Rules of Engagement, testing hours, and timeline. Written authorisation must be signed before anything else happens. This phase also establishes emergency contacts and the procedure for handling unexpected findings.

nodes.label: Reconnaissance
nodes.detail: Gather intelligence on the target using only public sources: DNS records, WHOIS, LinkedIn profiles, job postings, GitHub repositories, and subdomain enumeration. No packets are sent to the target yet — this is entirely passive.

nodes.label: Scanning
nodes.detail: Actively probe the target within scope: Nmap discovers open ports and services, Nessus or OpenVAS identifies known CVEs, Nikto checks web servers for common misconfigurations. This builds the vulnerability shortlist for exploitation.

nodes.label: Exploitation
nodes.detail: Attempt to exploit confirmed vulnerabilities to prove real-world impact. Every step is documented: commands run, timestamps, screenshots, and output logs. Only techniques within the agreed Rules of Engagement are permitted.

nodes.label: Reporting
nodes.detail: Deliver a structured report: executive summary for leadership, technical findings with CVSS severity scores, proof-of-concept evidence, and a prioritised remediation roadmap. The report is the entire value of the engagement.

caption: Click each phase to read what actually happens during it. Reporting feeds directly into the next Scoping session — VAPT is a continuous cycle, not a one-time event.
